$comment: Member kinds this lexicon supplies to a chant workspace (#3932). chant reads this file as data and never imports the lexicon. A dbt project reads the tables a sql member declares, so its kind ships beside them. Its reader, dbt-project, is chant's own code: it parses dbt_project.yml and the sources YAML under the model paths, never runs dbt, never renders Jinja and never reads profiles.yml, and turns each source table and column into a link to the sql member's <schema>.<table> and <schema>.<table>.<column> outputs (#3931). The same pass exposes each model as an output, <schema>.<model> and <schema>.<model>.<column> where the model's YAML lists columns (#3935); the schema is the modelSchema field, or the custom schema dbt config names when the project's generate_schema_name makes that independent of the target. Four more kinds read existing migration directories (#4400): goose, golang-migrate, clickhouse-migrations and flyway. Each has a probe and a reader (goose-dir, golang-migrate-dir, clickhouse-migrations-dir, flyway-dir) that lists the migrations in the order the tool applies them, with their dialect, and never runs the tool or a server. The reader returns no links and no outputs: the tables and columns a directory produces come from replaying it into a server, not from reading its files.

kinds.name: dbt
kinds.description: a dbt project, with a dbt_project.yml in its directory; its sources link to the tables and columns a sql member declares, its models are outputs other members link to, and dbt is never run

sqlMember.description: The member whose tables the project's sources read. Unset, each source table links to the one member that exposes it, and a table two members expose is ambiguous (WSP095).

dialect.description: How source names are cased before they are matched: postgres folds an unquoted name to lowercase and keeps a quoted one as written, the way dbt-postgres quotes a source's schema and identifier unless quoting turns it off; clickhouse keeps every name as written.

modelSchema.description: The schema the project's models land in. When set, each model is the output <modelSchema>.<model> and dbt's config is not read for the schema. Unset, chant reads +schema, the model YAML's config and the model's config(schema=...), and a model whose schema depends on the target (dbt's default generate_schema_name joins the target schema to a custom one) is reported as a gap (WSP099) that asks you to set this field.

kinds.name: goose
kinds.description: a goose migrations directory, with .sql files that carry -- +goose Up (and optionally -- +goose Down) sections; the migrations are listed in version order and goose is never run

dialect.description: The SQL dialect the migrations are written in. The tool takes it from a driver or URL the directory does not hold, so a goose or golang-migrate member names it; unset, postgres.

migrationsDir.description: The directory under the member's own that holds the migration files. Only the member's own directory is probed, so a member whose files sit in a subdirectory names its kind in its entry.

kinds.name: golang-migrate
kinds.description: a golang-migrate directory, with <version>_<name>.up.sql and .down.sql pairs; the up files are listed in version order and migrate is never run

dialect.description: The SQL dialect the migrations are written in. The tool takes it from a driver or URL the directory does not hold, so a goose or golang-migrate member names it; unset, postgres.

migrationsDir.description: The directory under the member's own that holds the migration files. Only the member's own directory is probed, so a member whose files sit in a subdirectory names its kind in its entry.

kinds.name: clickhouse-migrations
kinds.description: a directory for the Node or Python clickhouse-migrations tool, with <version>_<name>.sql files; they are listed in version order and the tool is never run

migrationsDir.description: The directory under the member's own that holds the migration files. Only the member's own directory is probed, so a member whose files sit in a subdirectory names its kind in its entry.

kinds.name: flyway
kinds.description: a Flyway project, with a flyway.toml or flyway.conf, or V<version>__<description>.sql files; the migrations of its locations are listed in the order flyway migrate applies them and Flyway is never run

dialect.description: The SQL dialect the migrations are written in. Unset, chant reads it from the JDBC URL in flyway.toml or flyway.conf, and falls back to postgres.
